title: Cities: Skylines | Franklin, Episode 11: Banking & Commerce
premise: The presenter connects early American currency, national-bank power and contradictions of democratic Greek Revival to Franklin/Philadelphia’s concentration of commerce and its eventual shift to New York.
coverage: Bank modeling, a projected architectural lecture, financial diagrams and city construction accompany early American banking history. Historical claims are the presenter’s. Brief inserts may be missed; cut times and musical cue boundaries are approximate.

panels.heading: Franklin opening
panels.description: Gold Franklin bell logo overlays oblique city views; the opening establishes the city whose financial geography will later be explained.
panels.camera: The viewpoint moves over the rooftops, and intro cuts show the city from different angles.
panels.action: Logo is superimposed; no presenter character is visible.

sound.text: Title music: Beethoven’s Symphony No. 5, IV. Allegro, performed by the Davis High School Symphony Orchestra.

panels.heading: JUST
panels.description: A slanted white sticker reading JUST with an orange star covers the center of the Hamilton poster title.
panels.camera: Static poster and sticker over the changing Blender viewport.
panels.action: A JUST sticker is added to the previously plain musical poster; the following panel changes the sticker to POST.
panels.visualGag: The middle beat of the Hamilton posting joke: the musical poster is relabeled JUST, with POST and the @publius handle still to come.
panels.notes: The larger slogan or reference is uncertain.

panels.heading: POST
panels.description: The Hamilton poster now bears a black POST sticker with a blue star instead of the previous white JUST sticker.
panels.camera: Static editorial poster/sticker; underlying Blender reference work continues.
panels.action: JUST changes to POST, followed by the three @publius portraits.
panels.visualGag: Payoff of the two sticker beats: JUST then POST makes the musical hero into a poster, connecting the narration about posting to the @publius social-media joke immediately afterward.

panels.heading: @publius
panels.description: Hamilton, Jay and Madison portraits appear under @publius, following the JUST and POST stickers on the musical poster.
panels.camera: Static insert over a Blender time-lapse. The viewport orbits, zooms and cuts between views.
panels.action: Architectural modeling continues behind changing cutouts and captions.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the JUST/POST poster relabeling: Hamilton’s posting becomes an @publius Twitter-style handle for the three pamphleteers, and the historical pamphlets become a massive tweet thread.

panels.heading: Burr’s revolver

panels.heading: Bank shot dead
panels.description: George Clinton portrait is juxtaposed with the upright First Bank photograph as its charter ends and the narrator says he shot Hamilton's bank dead; the next panel rotates the bank image sideways.
panels.camera: Static insert over a Blender time-lapse. The viewport orbits, zooms and cuts between views.
panels.action: Clinton and the upright bank set up the institution’s death metaphor; the photograph then turns sideways toward the right edge.
panels.visualGag: Connected setup for the bank-photo death payoff: “shot dead” extends the Burr, revolver and falling-Hamilton joke from the man to his institution. No second gun appears.

panels.heading: The bank falls sideways
panels.description: The First Bank photograph lies about 90 degrees sideways and partly leaves the right edge over Blender editing.
panels.camera: The bank photograph has rotated from its upright position; the architectural editing continues behind it.
panels.action: The photograph turns sideways and leaves the right side, echoing Hamilton's earlier portrait rotation. No new gun is visible.
panels.visualGag: Visual payoff to “he shot Hamilton’s bank dead”: the bank’s photograph repeats the slapstick of Hamilton’s falling portrait.
panels.notes: It is unclear whether the sideways photograph is a fall or a rotate-out transition.

panels.heading: Greek Revival lecture
panels.description: Projected title slide reads WILLIAM STRICKLAND, AMERICAN DEMOCRACY, AND GREEK REVIVAL above a temple-front building.
panels.camera: Cut from desktop to a black-framed projected slide that comes into focus.
panels.action: Static building photograph and title; no character action.
panels.visualGag: Mock lecture apparatus is sustained by soft-focus-to-sharp slide changes.

panels.heading: Direct Athenian democracy
panels.description: Assembly painting fills the projected slide as attendance, payment and sortition contrast with the founders’ representative institutions.
panels.camera: Cuts between projected slides, sometimes blurred before coming into focus.
panels.action: The slide holds on screen.
panels.visualGag: Visual setup for the later Knicks substitution: the static ancient assembly painting establishes Athens as the serious referent; the later New York Knicks logo interrupts this same image at the hill-name pun.

panels.heading: The undemocratic republic
panels.description: The same static assembly painting remains while indirect Senate elections and rich-versus-poor power become the point of comparison.
panels.camera: Cuts between projected slides, sometimes blurred before coming into focus.
panels.action: The slide holds on screen.
panels.visualGag: Continuation of the ancient-assembly visual setup. Its serious political discussion precedes the Knicks logo intruding on the same painting; the logo, not the painting alone, is the joke’s payoff.

panels.heading: Knicks on the hill

panels.camera: Cuts between projected slides, sometimes blurred before coming into focus.
panels.action: The slide holds on screen.
panels.visualGag: The Knicks logo makes a sound-alike joke about the assembly hill, apparently Pnyx.

panels.visualGag: A monumental elite building stands for Greek Revival’s claims to equality and democracy while the narrator says that “so naturally” the style goes on churches, plantation houses and banks. The picture shows the mismatch between the style’s ideals and its uses.

panels.heading: Convertibility circuit
panels.description: Treasury seal, national/private banks, individual icon, note and coins form a financial diagram over resumed Blender modeling.

panels.action: Banknote and coin illustrations move between labeled actors.

panels.heading: A dollar equals a dollar

panels.camera: Static insert over a Blender time-lapse. The viewport orbits, zooms and cuts between views.

panels.visualGag: Payoff to the convertibility circuit: the caption $1 = $1 REGARDLESS OF WHICH BANK ISSUED IT turns the hard-won monetary achievement into the absurd-sounding proposition that a dollar is worth one of itself.

panels.heading: Assets enter Franklin

panels.camera: Cut to overhead and oblique gameplay that zooms closer and rotates around the bank block.
panels.action: Building-selection previews turn into placed buildings.

panels.heading: Crisis beneath construction
panels.description: Second Bank occupies a larger plot while surrounding houses and streets are adjusted; narration traces crop/land price collapse and foreclosures.
panels.camera: The overhead viewpoint rotates and shifts between neighboring blocks.
panels.action: Buildings are selected, moved and placed; lots are cleared.

panels.camera: Gameplay zooms out, then shifts and rotates above exchange and banks.
panels.action: Exchange building is placed; nearby road geometry and buildings are adjusted.

panels.camera: The gameplay view zooms, rotates and shifts between oblique and overhead angles.
panels.action: Construction and detailing continue under the editorial overlays.

panels.action: The player keeps placing and detailing buildings, streets and market props.

panels.heading: The presidential alligator

panels.action: The alligator insert covers much of the logo while the canal image remains alongside it, interrupting the infrastructure montage.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the infrastructure setup: he also kept an alligator at the White House is illustrated literally with an absurd animal photograph amid railroad and canal pictures. The serious policy list becomes presidential trivia.
